claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi is an example of a high-entropy-alloy nanoparticle system relevant to the hypothesis.
Annealing or other thermal treatments can introduce atomic ordering in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Premelting and melting behavior is governed by an interplay among atomic ordering, grain-boundary and surface-energy effects, and lattice distortions.
Atomic ordering affects the energy landscape and atomic mobility of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Grain-boundary and surface-energy effects affect the energy landscape and atomic mobility of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Lattice distortions affect the energy landscape and atomic mobility of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Increasing atomic ordering raises the melting point.
Increasing atomic ordering reduces premelting behavior.
Reducing particle size raises the melting point.
Reducing particle size reduces premelting behavior.
The effects attributed to increased ordering and reduced particle size arise from enhanced energy barriers and reduced atomic mobility.
Increasing lattice distortion lowers the melting point.
Increasing lattice distortion produces more pronounced premelting behavior.
The effects attributed to lattice distortion arise from enhanced atomic mobility and reduced energy barriers.
The proposed relationships should hold across high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles having varied ordering, size, and composition when heating rate and atmosphere are controlled.
